questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding referral questions for psychological testing describe good practice except:

options.text: Referral for assessment of a child’s developmental process.
Referral for assessment of a child’s intellectual capacity and academic achievement.
Referral for clarification of a child’s diagnoses and assistance with therapeutic interventions.
Referral questions should be explained to the parents.
Referral questions should be formulated by the testing clinician after evaluation.

correct_answer.text: Referral questions should be formulated by the testing clinician after evaluation.

correct_answers.text: Referral questions should be formulated by the testing clinician after evaluation.

questions.explanation: To ensure the efficiency and efficacy of the assessment, it is critical to develop a list of referral questions to be answered by the psychological evaluations. The specific relevant referral questions should be formulated by the referring clinician and explained to the parents of the child being assessed. Several areas referral questions commonly address are: assessments of developmental process, intellectual capacity, academic achievement, learning disabilities, diagnoses, treatments, and prediction of course of treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best definition of construct validity on a testing instrument?

options.text: The test’s capacity to measure what it is supposed to measure (such as underlying theoretical, intangible qualities or traits in which individuals differ)
The test’s effectiveness in predicting an individual’s performance in specific areas
The fact that the test’s content covers a representative sample for the property being measured
The degree to which the test results can be reproduced
Pretesting of the test on a large, demographically representative group of individuals

correct_answer.text: The test’s capacity to measure what it is supposed to measure (such as underlying theoretical, intangible qualities or traits in which individuals differ)

correct_answers.text: The test’s capacity to measure what it is supposed to measure (such as underlying theoretical, intangible qualities or traits in which individuals differ)

questions.explanation: Answer (b) defines criterion-related validity, answer (c) defines content validity, answer (d) defines reliability, and answer (e) defines standardization. It is important to know the reliability and validity of a particular test in interpreting the results.

questions.question_text: All of the following intelligence tests can be used in younger children (<4 years) except:

options.text: Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (KABC-2)
Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence, Third Edition (WPPSI-III)

questions.explanation: The Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence (WASI) is designed to be used for individuals age 6:0 to 89:0 years of age. The DAS-II is designed for children age 2:6 to 17:11 years, the KABC-2 for children age 3:0 to 18:11 years, the SB-5 for children age 2:0 to adults age 89:11 years, and the WPPSI for those age 2:6 to 7:3.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Second Edition are accurate except:

options.text: It is an excellent measurement of adaptive behavior.
It can be used in individuals with cognitive delay.
It can be completed by the child’s teacher.

questions.explanation: The Vineland does not measure academic achievement, as does the Woodcock-Johnson Psychoeducational Battery or the Wide Range Achievement Test. Many factors can influence the assessment of adaptive functioning, and there is some reported fluctuation in means and standard deviations across age groups with the Vineland. It does come with a teacher form.

questions.question_text: The Rorschach inkblots can be used for children as young as:
questions.explanation: Besides the Thematic Apperception Test, the Rorschach is also a projective test. It is used to assess personality organization and provides data regarding the child’s developmental capacities for reality testing, integration of affect, and maturational level of object relations in children as young as five years. It can be used to evaluate personality development, and help to reveal children’s hidden emotions or internal conflicts.

questions.question_text: All of the following are projective assessment procedures that can be used in children except:
questions.explanation: The Children Personality Questionnaire (CPQ) is one of the objective personality measures for children among others including: High School Personality Questionnaire (HSPQ), Millon Adolescent Personality Inventory (MAPI), Millon Adolescent Clinical Inventory (MACI), Millon Pre-Adolescent Clinical Inventory (M-PACI), Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory, Adolescent (MMPI-A), and Personality Inventory for Children, Second Edition (PIC-2). Besides all the listed projective measures other such measures may include Projective Drawings, Roberts Apperception Test for Children, Second Edition (Roberts-2), and Rorschach inkblot tests.

questions.question_text: All of the following instruments can be used during early infancy except:
questions.explanation: The Draw-A-Person Test (DAP) can be used as a projective test in subjects 5–17 years. The other tests listed are measures of neonate, infant, and toddler development, and can all be used during early infancy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following instruments has the best performance data and the greatest usage in measuring childhood behavior problems?

options.text: Missouri Assessment of Genetics Interview for Children (MAGIC)
Child Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (K-SADS)
Diagnostic Interview Schedule for Children and Adolescents (DICA)
Interview Schedule for Children and Adolescents (ISCA)

questions.explanation: The CBCL has been considered a gold standard among behavioral rating scales. It is validated and is the most widely used instrument in research and clinical settings to measure a range of internalizing and externalizing behaviors. The K-SADS, MAGIC, ISCA, and DICA are diagnostic interviews, not behavior rating scales.

questions.question_text: Neuropsychological evaluation is useful in the assessment of all of the following areas except:
questions.explanation: Variability in cerebral organization makes it impossible to determine that one specific brain region is involved or damaged, especially using one particular test. Neuropsychological testing is rarely used to find the “site of lesion” and brain regions are interrelated in a manner that makes it very unlikely that only one particular brain region is involved. All other areas listed are commonly assessed through neuropsychological testing.

questions.question_text: All of the following areas can be reliably assessed in children and adolescents using psychological tests except:
questions.explanation: Psychological testing cannot assess life expectancy. All other listed areas can be reliably assessed by psychological testing. Psychological testing can also provide concrete, standardized data about language skills, visual-motor coordination, developmental level, neurocognitive functioning, and occupational interest and aptitude.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding intelligence tests is inaccurate?

options.text: Intelligence tests measure both a global/overall capacity and separate/subscale abilities.
IQ score is not used to determine severity of intellectual disability in DSM-5.
The most widely used tests to assess intelligence and cognitive functioning are the Wechsler scales.
Individuals’ IQ scores demonstrate wide variability after the age of 5 years.
IQ testing can be used to assist making diagnoses of specific learning disabilities.

correct_answer.text: Individuals’ IQ scores demonstrate wide variability after the age of 5 years.

correct_answers.text: Individuals’ IQ scores demonstrate wide variability after the age of 5 years.

questions.explanation: Individual IQ scores are relatively stable after about age five, although there may be individual differences. The Wechsler scales are most widely used for testing intellectual functioning. IQ score per se is no longer used as a diagnostic criterion for intellectual disability in DSM-5 (in contrast to DSM-IV). The severity of the intellectual disability is based on adaptive functioning, but not IQ scores. Deficits of intellectual functioning must be confirmed by both clinical assessment and individualized, standardized intelligence testing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a nonverbal and language-free test?
questions.explanation: McCarthy Scales of Early Learning (MSEL) is an intelligence test consisting of six scales including verbal, perceptual performance, quantitative, general cognitive, memory, and motor. It is a good assessment tool for measuring general strength and weakness in young children. The other listed instruments are all considered as nonverbal and language free or culture free.

questions.question_text: All of the following are achievement tests except:

options.text: Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement, Second Edition (KTEA-II)
Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (KABC-II)
Wide Range Achievement Test, Fourth Edition (WRAT4)
Woodcock-Johnson, Third Edition Test of Achievement (WJ III ACH)

correct_answer.text: Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (KABC-II)

correct_answers.text: Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (KABC-II)

questions.explanation: The Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (KABC-II) is not an achievement test. Instead, it is an intelligence test that consists of subtests including measures of sequential and simultaneous processing, fluid reasoning and crystallized ability, and long-term retrieval. Most of the intellectual, achievement, and processing tests are structured in a similar way using 100 as the mean score and 15 as the standard deviation in order to be compared across instruments.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tests can be only used for assessing receptive language but not expressive language?
questions.explanation: The Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test (PPVT) can be used only to assess receptive language. The rest of the tests listed can be used to assess both receptive and expressive language.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tests is not a commonly used projective test for clinical hypothesis generation?
questions.explanation: The Wisconsin card sorting test (not a projective test) is used to measure executive functioning and attention capacity. All of the other tests listed are projective tests useful for generating clinical hypotheses regarding children’s feelings about themselves and their families. The information generated needs to be integrated into the clinical evaluation and cannot be used alone.

questions.question_text: Which of the following objective personality measures can be administered to children as young as five years old?

options.text: Personality Inventory for Children, Second Edition (PIC-2)

correct_answer.text: Personality Inventory for Children, Second Edition (PIC-2)

correct_answers.text: Personality Inventory for Children, Second Edition (PIC-2)

questions.explanation: The Personality Inventory for Children, Second Edition (PIC-2) can be administered for youth between the ages of 5 and 19 years. The M-PCI is for older children (between the ages of 9 and 12 years), and so is the Children’s Personality Questionnaire (CPQ) (between the ages of 8 and 13 years). In addition to the High School Personality Questionnaire (HSPQ), the rest of the listed tests are all for adolescents.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an instrument based on interviewing the parents and the parents’ reports for assessment of communication?
questions.explanation: The Denver II is administered by the clinician/examiner, and is not based on the parents’ report. The rest of the listed instruments are used for assessing communication based on interviewing the parents and the parents’ report.

questions.question_text: All of the following are considered as interrelated and interdependent domains of executive function except:
questions.explanation: Attention control (e.g., selective attention, self-regulation, self-monitoring, and inhibition), cognitive flexibility (e.g., divided attention, working memory, conceptual transfer, and feedback utilization), goal setting (e.g., initiative, conceptual reasoning, planning, and strategy organization), information processing (e.g., efficiency, fluency, and speed of processing) are four domains of executive function in children and adolescents.

questions.question_text: Which of the following reliability concepts is measured by the consistency obtained by the same person who takes the same test on two different occasions?
questions.explanation: Test-retest reliability is measured and obtained by the same person taking the same test on two different occasions. On the other hand, the interrater reliability is obtained by getting the same results when the same test is administered by different examiners.

questions.question_text: Which of the following T-scores is equivalent to a typical mean score of 100?
questions.explanation: A T-score of 50 is equivalent to a typical standard mean score of 100. Standard scores are very useful for making comparisons across tests. Thus, most cognitive and achievement tests use standard mean scores of 100 with a standard deviation of 15. However, many behavioral checklists use T-scores that have a mean of 50 with a standard deviation of 10.

questions.question_text: Bayley-III
questions.explanation: The Bayley among others such as the Halstead-Reitan Neuropsychological Test Battery, Second Edition, the Luria-Nebraska Neuropsychological Battery, and NEPSY-II are all comprehensive neuropsychological batteries that have been developed to assess across multiple neurological systems.

questions.question_text: Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence, Third Edition (WPPSI-III)
questions.explanation: The WPPSI-III is intended for use in children age 2:6–7:3 years.

questions.question_text: Conners’ Rating Scale, Revised (CRS-R)
questions.explanation: The Conners’ Rating Scale-Revised is a measure of externalizing behaviors and is best known for use in the assessment of ADHD.

questions.question_text: Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL)
questions.explanation: The CBCL uses factor-derived scores to classify behaviors as externalizing or internalizing. It has been the gold standard for research and clinical work among broad-band behavior rating scales.

questions.question_text: Children’s Depression Inventory (CDI)
questions.explanation: The CDI is derived from the adult Beck Depression Inventory, written at first grade level and used in both young children and teenagers.

questions.question_text: Practice effects

options.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance
Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores
Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

correct_answer.text: Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

correct_answers.text: Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

questions.explanation: Practice effects refer to improved scores due to familiarity with or prior exposure to the test items.

questions.question_text: Item content differences

options.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance
Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores
Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

correct_answer.text: Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores

correct_answers.text: Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores

questions.explanation: Item content differences refer to the differences in the measures of the content.

questions.question_text: Ceiling effects

options.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance
Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores
Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

questions.explanation: Ceiling effects occur when there are not enough hard items.

questions.question_text: Floor effects

options.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance
Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores
Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

questions.explanation: Floor effects occur when there are not enough easy items.

questions.question_text: The Flynn effect

options.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance
Effects of level of language, memory, and speed of processing on the overall IQ scores
Improvement of the score due to the familiarity of the test

correct_answer.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance

correct_answers.text: Continued rise in IQ test performance

questions.explanation: The Flynn effect refers to the continuous increase in IQ performance over years.
